text:
Situation: Ketorolac tromethamine has been on FDA's drug shortage list since 2018-03-23 and remains current as of 2026-10-21. Baxter Healthcare and Fresenius Kabi also appear on the list with current status and estimated recoveries in late 2026. Our combined inventory across five sites totals approximately 1,374 units, providing 11.2 to 23.7 days of supply per location.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the shortage on 2018-03-23. Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1925262) is a registered plant on the product label. That plant had an OAI inspection ending 2016-06-08 (653 days before the posting), a Warning Letter issued 2017-02-14 (402 days before the posting), and another OAI inspection ending 2018-08-15 with a classification letter dated 2020-04-22 (145 days after the posting). FDA's shortage list does not state that these inspection outcomes caused the shortage.

Our position: Current stock is insufficient to sustain operations through the projected recovery window. The rule-ranked alternate supplier, A-S Medication Solutions, is not on FDA's shortage list today. Four additional suppliers are also not on the shortage list. None of the five alternate labels name a plant we could verify.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer initiates purchase agreements with A-S Medication Solutions; requires P&T committee approval.
2. Buyer qualifies Advanced Rx of Tennessee, LLC as a secondary source; requires P&T committee approval.
3. Buyer qualifies Anthea Pharma Private Limited as a tertiary source; requires P&T committee approval.
4. Buyer qualifies Camber Pharmaceuticals, Inc. as a quaternary source; requires P&T committee approval.
5. Buyer qualifies Caplin Steriles Limited as a quinary source; requires P&T committee approval.

Not recommended: Delaying procurement until current inventory falls below seven days at any site.
